title: I. Short Permutation Problem
statement:
You are given an integer n.

For each (m, k) such that 3 ≤ m ≤ n+1 and 0 ≤ k ≤ n-1, count the permutations of [1, 2, ..., n] such that p_i + p_{i+1} ≥ m for exactly k indices i, modulo 998,244,353.

The input consists of a single line, which contains two integers n, x (2 ≤ n ≤ 4000, 1 ≤ x < 1,000,000,007).

Let a_{m,k} be the answer for the pair (m, k), modulo 998,244,353.

Let large S = ∑_{m=3}^{n+1} ∑_{k=0}^{n-1} a_{m,k}x^{mn+k}phantom0.

Output a single line with an integer: S modulo 1,000,000,007.

Note that using two different modulos is intentional. We want you to calculate all the a_{m,k} modulo 998,244,353, then treat them like integers in the range [0, 998,244,352], and hash them modulo 1,000,000,007.
